comment: Written from the maker's source at commit 7f2d7f2 (the plugin.json carrying 2.0.1); head carries the same source. Thirteen of the fourteen inputs are configured with an empty name, so every input tooltip except the sine-square jack's is blank; the five outputs are all configured with empty names as well. Two polyphony faults are in the shipped code. In process(), the sync handling indexes engine.syncCheck[c+i] and engine.phase[c+i] with the absolute channel number rather than the lane number, so beyond the first four channels it reads and writes past the ends of a four-element array and a float_4; sync is correct on channels 1 to 4 only. In scanReturn(), the search index i is declared outside the loop over the four lanes and so is never reset between them, and the early return for a lane whose scan value falls in the first region returns that one divisor for all four lanes; with different scan voltages per channel the divisor chosen for the later channels can be wrong. The low output takes scanReturn at a scan value of 1, which is the largest active divisor and therefore the lowest pitch, matching what the README means by 'lowest'. The scan value fed to the divisor lookup is unclamped while the reflected scan value is clamped to 0 to 1; the lookup is bounded either way, so a scan input above 10V parks on the highest divisor.
